BrickLane Retailers - Q3 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the BrickLane Retailers Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss BrickLane Retailers' results for the third quarter. Joining me on today’s call are Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Ramirez, Chief Merchandising Officer; Emily Carter, Chief Stores Officer; Alex Patel, Chief Marketing Officer; and Jordan Lee, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Mike Thompson.

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report BrickLane Retailers' performance for the third quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

Our comparable sales, which we often refer to as comps, measure the performance from our mature store base—locations open at least 52 weeks—net of remodel disruptions longer than two weeks, and excluding fuel and non-merchandise sales. This remains our key indicator for organic growth across our more than 1,200 locations in the U.S. and Canada. In Q3, we achieved comps of plus 2.8 percent, surpassing our guidance of flat to plus 2 percent. This was powered by a 1.2 percent rise in traffic—the first positive traffic reading since the first quarter of 2023—along with a solid 1.5 percent increase in average unit retail from our fall private label offerings, such as the Urban Forge apparel collection and Haven Home essentials. Units per transaction stayed stable at 2.1, while conversion rose 50 basis points to 28 percent, thanks to our updated in-store digital kiosks now in 40 percent of stores, which are lifting add-on sales by 15 percent on average.

Moving forward, for the fourth quarter ending January 2025, we are guiding comps to the plus 3 to plus 5 percent range. This builds on the gradual traffic recovery, with projections of plus 1 to plus 2 percent foot traffic, driven by holiday merchandising and the BrickLane Black Friday Blitz loyalty effort, which last year spiked enrollments by 22 percent and boosted repeat visits 18 percent year over year. Average unit retail should grow another 1.5 to 2 percent, backed by smart pricing in core areas—apparel up 2 percent, home goods steady—as we compare against last year's heavy promotions in a lower-inflation setting. We factor in holiday patterns, with December poised for plus 5 to plus 7 percent comps, much like Target's holiday results. Tailwinds include our store optimization, with 150 remodels completed year to date emphasizing urban and suburban high-traffic spots with shop-in-shop setups for beauty and athleisure partners, including our Fabletics exclusive. These are yielding a plus 4.2 percent comp lift in the first full post-refresh quarter. Our AI planogram tool, now in 60 percent of stores, optimizes high-margin shelf space, cutting out-of-stocks 12 percent and improving conversion 80 basis points.

By region, the Sunbelt—Florida, Texas, Carolinas—should see plus 6 to plus 8 percent, thanks to weather and migration trends. Midwest and Northeast may trail at plus 1 to plus 3 percent due to weather and discretionary softness, similar to Dick's Sporting Goods' comments. Canada shines at plus 4 percent with Toronto flagship growth. Headwinds like tepid consumer sentiment, especially among our core 35-to-54-year-olds facing 3.5 percent CPI on basics, are offset by everyday low prices on 20 percent of stock, maintaining 38.5 percent gross margins in Q3 while growing units 2 percent. Memphis DC upgrades keep freight flat despite Red Sea issues. For full fiscal 2025, we are raising comp guidance to plus 4 to plus 6 percent from prior plus 3 to plus 5 percent, with Q1 at plus 3 to plus 4 percent via the Refresh Renewal campaign linking traffic to BOPIS, now 18 percent of digital sales and adding plus 2.5 percent to store comps. Inventory is tight at 13 weeks, down 8 percent year over year, shrink at 1.4 percent with RFID in 70 percent of doors. This aligns with our stores-first approach, investing $250 million in CapEx for 100 small-format stores in Phoenix and Atlanta, while digital comps guide at plus 12 to plus 15 percent without major store cannibalization. We sit ahead of Macy's plus 1 to plus 2 percent outlook and match TJX's mid-single digits, with better AUR from owned brands at 42 percent of sales. This assumes no big consumer or geopolitical shifts.

E-commerce was another standout, growing 18.4 percent year over year to $1.2 billion, marking 11 straight quarters of double-digit gains and lifting digital to 28 percent of total sales, up from 22 percent and matching Macy's and Kohl's progress. While overall comps were plus 0.2 percent amid inflation and discretionary caution—stores down 1.5 percent in apparel—digital outpaced the NRSC's 6-to-8 percent industry average. Traffic jumped 22 percent via 35 percent better organic search from Google Cloud NLP site optimization, like Wayfair's approach. Conversion hit 3.8 percent from Adobe personalization using myBrickLane loyalty data, boosting add-to-cart 12 percent and average order value 9 percent to $128 in activewear and decor. Mobile took 62 percent of traffic, app orders up 31 percent with Shop & Scan AR converting 15 percent higher for Gen Z impulse buys. Sunbelt digital grew 25 percent via DoorDash/Instacart same-day, Northeast 14 percent on 42 percent BOPIS like Target. Canada/UK DTC up 42 percent on small base. Home goods led at 24 percent, apparel 16 percent, electronics 11 percent. $150 million investment in headless BigCommerce enabled sub-2-second loads and store integration; micro-DCs cut next-day to 85 percent coverage, costs to $4.20 per order. Symbiotic with stores—68 percent digital shoppers visit physical within a week, lifting CLV 22 percent. Q3 guide 15-to-17 percent, full-year $5.1-to-5.3 billion at 19 percent growth, margins to 42.5 percent.

Store productivity remains strong, with sales per square foot at $342, up 4.2 percent year over year from $328, the 11th straight quarter of gains and a 6.1 percent three-year CAGR, stacked plus 12.7 percent beating S&P retail index 8.2 percent. Trailing 12-month at $1,378. Apparel led at $415, up 7.1 percent from Fast Fashion Refresh capsules turning 4.8 times. Home at $298, up 2.9 percent with Maker's Lab demos converting 15 percent higher on big-ticket. Footwear $267 flat on sneaker trends like Nike/Foot Locker. Sunbelt $378 up 8.6 percent with 14 new 15,000-sq-ft prototypes 25 percent better than big boxes. Northeast $305 down 1.2 percent on mall vacancies; Midwest $331 steady. Right-Sizing playbook remodeled 320 stores, shifting 18 percent space to hero zones at $512 SPSF with 28 percent omnichannel sales. SymphonyAI planograms up precision 22 percent, stockouts down 35 percent, plus $24 per store; RFID pilots cut shrink 40 percent. Q3 guide $345-to-350, 3-to-5 percent growth. CapEx $450 million targets $375 by FY26.

Progress on key strategic initiatives across our four pillars—store optimization, omnichannel, supply chain, customer innovation—is accelerating same-store growth to 4.8 percent versus industry 2.1 percent NRF. Store optimization finished 85 percent of 2023 remodels, 142 NextGen formats with AR mirrors lifting comps 12.3 percent, traffic 8.2 percent; closed 28 low-NOI sites saving $45 million; 35 new express stores in Sunbelt. Southeast 6.1 percent comps, Midwest flat. Omnichannel BOPIS 28 percent of digital, 72 percent conversion; same-day in 65 percent DMAs via DoorDash, digital 42 percent of revenue; Unified Commerce cut ship times 37 percent, costs $3.45, added 150 bps margins. Supply chain: 41 percent Mexico/Vietnam sourcing down costs 9 percent; Reno DC throughput 55 percent to 250,000 cases, 99.2 percent accuracy, turns 5.8x. Customer innovation: Peak Rewards 18.7 million members up 24 percent, 42 percent redemption via Google BigQuery AI, basket up 15 percent; private Urban Essentials up 31 percent to $280 million; 65 percent sustainable assortment, Scope 1 down 22 percent. ROI 18.2 percent on $450 million CapEx, $75 million EBITDA add FY24; UK pilot +7.2 percent.

Inventory levels ended at $1.18 billion, down 22 percent year over year from $1.52 billion—fifth straight decline, lowest since pre-pandemic. Comparable basis down 19 percent excluding closures; turns 5.3x from 4.1x, weeks 12.4 from 16.8. Apparel down 28 percent to $532 million on 72 percent full-price sell-through, cut spring buys 30 percent. Footwear down 8 percent to $285 million, athleisure 7.2x turns. Home up 5 percent to $354 million for holidays. Northeast down 25 percent to $410 million, 11.2 weeks; Southeast 15 percent to $320 million, 13.8 weeks post-hurricane; West 20 percent to $280 million, California sub-11 weeks; Canada 18 percent to $95 million. Blue Yonder AI forecasting 92 percent accurate, safety stock down 18 percent; RFID 65 percent high-value, shrink down 22 percent; VMI 25 percent flow. SKU cull 15 percent to 28,000, 82 percent sales high performers; store e-com 28 percent digital. Q4 trough $1.1 billion, 8-to-10 percent down, 5.5x turns.

Shrink and theft pressured gross margins this quarter, a persistent challenge in brick-and-mortar encompassing shoplifting, organized retail crime, employee issues, errors, and fraud—eroding COGS. Gross margin at 34.2 percent, down 110 bps year over year from 35.3 percent; ex-shrink, underlying up 20 bps to 36.1 percent on mix and pricing. Shrink dragged 130 bps, up from 90 bps, $185 million or 1.95 percent sales—highest since Q1 2022. Aligns 2023 1.7 percent with NRF 1.6 percent benchmark, but up on ORC. Electronics and beauty 45 percent shrink dollars on 22 percent sales, via barcode swaps to online fences like Target/Walmart issues. West Coast over 2.4 percent, up 35 percent on Prop 47; 150 ORC in LA/Bay. Midwest/Southeast 1.4-to-1.6 percent. Countering with AI video analytics in 450 stores, 92 percent accuracy down incidents 22 percent; RFID source tagging 65 percent to 85 percent, cut sweethearting 18 percent; SCO verification down 15 percent; RILA intel sharing, 25 ex-LAPD task force. Omnichannel ship-from-store 28 percent e-com reduces exposure; Texas pilots with locked cases up conversion 8 percent. Q4 to 1.8 percent, full-year 110 bps drag; $120 million CapEx 4x return, target 35.5 percent+ 2025.

Markdowns also impacted margins, at 14.8 percent of sales versus 12.1 percent last year, up 270 bps but down 50 bps sequentially post-2022 overhang. Apparel 18.2 percent on casual/active soft; footwear 13.4 percent post-athleisure cool; home 10.1 percent steady. 140 bps margin hit in 38.2 percent gross, down 200 bps total with freight/mix; underlying 39.5 percent beats Macy's/Kohl's. Northeast/Midwest 16.5 percent on weather; Sunbelt 12.7 percent. Inventory flat YoY per sq ft, 14.2 weeks vs 15.8, turns 4.1x. Blue Yonder 92 percent forecast down overbuy 15 percent; vendor rebates $25 million; private label to 28 percent, 500-700 bps richer; ship-from-store 35 percent e-com up velocity 22 percent. Q3 13.5 percent markdowns, margins 39.0 percent; full-year 38.5-to-39.0 percent.

We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to provide more details on our financial results.

Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Mike. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the third quarter.

Our total revenue for the quarter was $7.2 billion, a 3.5 percent increase compared to the same period last year. Gross margin was 36.5 percent, primarily driven by favorable product mix shifts, lower freight from efficiencies, and private label expansion, though tempered by shrink and markdowns as Mike noted. Operating expenses were $2.1 billion, representing 29.2 percent of revenue, reflecting disciplined cost control and productivity gains. Net income was $450 million, or $1.25 per share. We generated $650 million in cash flow from operations. Inventory levels are currently lean at 13 weeks of supply, down 8 percent year over year.

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet and are well positioned to invest in our growth initiatives.

Now, I'd like to hand it over to David Ramirez, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines, followed by Emily Carter to discuss store operations, Alex Patel to discuss marketing initiatives, and Jordan Lee to talk about technology advancements.

David Ramirez, Chief Merchandising Officer:
Thank you, Lisa. This quarter, we launched our Urban Forge apparel line, which has seen strong uptake with sell-through rates exceeding 85 percent at full price and contributing over $150 million in incremental sales. We are excited about the potential of this new product and other upcoming launches like expanded Haven Home essentials.

Emily Carter, Chief Stores Officer:
Thank you, David. We continue to focus on improving the customer experience in our stores. We have implemented NextGen remodels with AR try-on mirrors and experiential zones in 142 locations, delivering 12.3 percent comp lifts and 8.2 percent traffic gains, and are seeing positive results across Sunbelt and urban formats.

Alex Patel, Chief Marketing Officer:
Thank you, Emily. Our BrickLane Black Friday Blitz campaign, tied to Peak Rewards loyalty, has increased brand awareness by 25 percent and driven 22 percent enrollment growth, with members spending 4 times more.

Jordan Lee, Chief Technology Officer:
Thank you, Alex. We have invested in AI-powered planogram optimization and video analytics now in 60 percent and 450 stores respectively, which has improved shelf productivity, reduced out-of-stocks by 12 percent, and cut theft incidents 22 percent.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your sales?

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Good question, John. Inflation has hit our core middle-income demo hard, with 3.5 percent CPI on essentials shifting focus to value. We've countered with everyday low prices on 20 percent of inventory, growing units 2 percent while holding margins at 38.5 percent, and private labels up 150 basis points to 28 percent penetration.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
For Q4, we're guiding comps to plus 3 to plus 5 percent, assuming plus 1 to plus 2 percent traffic from holidays and loyalty, plus 1.5 to 2 percent AUR, with strength in Sunbelt and December acceleration.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Kim (Morgan Stanley):
Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements?

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Absolutely. Our Reno DC with AutoStore and AI slotting boosted throughput 55 percent to 250,000 cases daily at 99.2 percent accuracy. Nearshoring to 41 percent Mexico/Vietnam cut costs 9 percent despite Red Sea, with 97 percent on-time delivery.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Green with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Rachel Green (Barclays):
What is the impact from the loyalty program?

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Peak Rewards, with 18.7 million members up 24 percent, drives 42 percent redemptions via AI personalization, 15 percent higher baskets, and 4 times spend versus non-members, adding plus 2.5 percent to store comps through BOPIS ties.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Rivera with Citi. Please go ahead.

Tom Rivera (Citi):
Regarding guidance assumptions, any changes to macro views?

Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Our FY25 revenue guide is $28.5 to $29.2 billion, 4 to 6 percent growth, comps 2.5 to 4 percent, op income $2.1 to $2.25 billion at 7.3 to 7.7 percent margin, EPS $4.80 to $5.10. Assumes CPI 2.2 percent, rates 3.8 to 4.2 percent, unemployment 4.2 percent, traffic up 1 to 2.5 percent, ASP 1.5 to 2 percent. Gross margin up 25 to 50 bps on freight down 10 to 12 percent, shrink to 1.6 percent, private labels $3.2 billion at 45 percent margins. SG&A 28.5 to 28.8 percent, CapEx $1.1 billion for fulfillment and remodels. No major tariffs, but contingencies ready.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes the question-and-answer session. I'll now turn the call back over to Mike Thompson for closing remarks.

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.

Impact of shrink/theft on gross margin
Markdown activity and its effect on margin

aspect_summary.Comp sales guidance for next quarter/yea: Q4: +3% to +5%; FY2025: raised to +4% to +6% (from prior +3% to +5%), with Q1 at +3% to +4%. (Note: Q&A mentions FY25 comps +2.5% to +4%.
aspect_summary.Key assumptions underlying guidance: Q4: +1-2% traffic from holidays/loyalty, +1.5-2% AUR, Sunbelt strength/December acceleration, store remodels/AI tools, no major consumer/geopolitical shifts. FY25: CPI 2.2%, rates 3.8-4.2%, unemployment 4.2%, traffic +1-2.5%, AUR/ASP +1.5-2%.
aspect_summary.Impact of shrink/theft on gross margin: Shrink at 1.95% of sales ($185M), dragged margins 130 bps (up from 90 bps); Q3 gross margin 34.2% (down 110 bps YoY), ex-shrink up 20 bps to 36.1%. Q4 shrink to 1.8%, full-year 110 bps drag; countered with AI/RFID/SCO measures.
aspect_summary.Sales per square foot: Q3: $342, +4.2% YoY from $328 (11th straight quarter gain, 6.1% 3-yr CAGR). Q3 guide $345-350 (+3-5%); FY26 target $375.
aspect_summary.E-commerce sales growth (YoY): Q3: +18.4% to $1.2B (digital 28% of sales, up from 22%; 11th straight double-digit quarter). Q3 guide +15-17%; FY: $5.1-5.3B at +19%.
aspect_summary.Markdown activity and its effect on marg: Q3: 14.8% of sales (vs 12.1% YoY, +270 bps), 140 bps margin hit (total down 200 bps with freight/mix); underlying 39.5%. Q3 guide 13.5%, margins 39.0%; FY 38.5-39.0%. Apparel/footwear led increases.
aspect_summary.Key strategic initiatives update: Store optimization: 142 NextGen remodels (+12.3% comps), 28 closures, 35 new express stores. Omnichannel: BOPIS 28% of digital (72% conversion), same-day delivery. Supply chain: 41% Mexico/Vietnam sourcing (-9% costs), Reno DC +55% throughput. Customer innovation: Peak Rewards 18.7M members (+24%, +15% basket), private labels +31%.
aspect_summary.Inventory levels (YoY): Q3 end: $1.18B, -22% YoY from $1.52B (5th straight decline, lowest pre-pandemic); 13 weeks (-8% YoY), turns 5.3x (from 4.1x), comparable -19%. Apparel -28%, home +5%. Q4 trough $1.1B (-8-10%).
